# Set79 Path A: existing-wallet DAILY worker to scheduled payment

Proposed finite actual acceptance; not executed. Root owns qualification and runtime. This complements Path B (`../public-daily-actual/PLAN.md`): Path A proves the original local wallet/vault signer and automatic worker; Path B proves the unseen late winner and immutable reserved payout across operator restart. Neither replaces the other. No new product API, login, native UI or D74 work is proposed.

## Reuse and original owners

Adapt `set74-prep/remote-attachment-actual/{main.go,fixture_helpers.go,run.py}` and its public `fixture-catalog.json` / `fixture-public.json`. Reuse the successful baseline6 copy rules, exact existing-wallet constructor, public row audit, original-view checks, stopped reopen and source-tree finalization. Reuse the Set79 Path B original daily runtime construction, real node helpers and bounded process ownership; do not copy its delayed-winner flow or observation fault into this case. A separate external probe module under `github.com/taytr-llc/slug/desktop/` can compose these actual APIs without exposing new product accessors.

The baseline6 `incrementing256` account has the established schema14 wallet, hosted vault, native84 recipient and signed fixture login. `zero256` has an intentional reset hold: preserve its entire wallet and hold; do not log it in or clear it. Retain both configured remote enrollments, but mine and receive payment only as incrementing256. This is one concrete attached wallet, not acceptance for both wallets or arbitrary authentication.

Before opening anything, copy the complete closed owned root and the two original chain directories into three independently owned scratch trees using the existing catalog checks: no symlinks/hardlinks, repairs or source opens as live databases. Keep all original files unchanged. In the copy, retain the old source, recipient INTENT/READY, allocation/guard, old worker outboxes and V1 ownership/league/financial histories byte-for-byte. Admit only the predecessor's explicitly selected account/vault login metadata, selected wallet synchronization and inventory reopen changes. New remote attachment, daily operator and schema16 custody use fresh separate roots. The original local HTTP127.0.0.1:explicit-port node boundary remains unchanged.

Actual ownership chain:

- `accountpilot.OpenDailyRemotePoolController` → original fixture Login → concrete `OwnedWalletSession`/View/Mining lease and private vault signer → `OpenDailyRemotePoolAttachment` → protected pool/admission clients → `NewDailyPool` and daily outbox.
- `pooloperator.CreateDaily`/Run → original online role owner, dedicated daily schema16 wallet/backend, Source2, Round2, indexed ledger2, actual daily scheduler and TLS ingress. The same original pointers remain attached until joined Close.

No signer callback, fabricated accepted row, direct ledger RunDaily, clock substitution, changed hash function or checkpoint secret is allowed. Online fixture custody uses only the already published three role recipes; the schema16 funding root remains the separately published leading-zero-account fixture. The selected local signer comes only from its existing vault/session.

## Independently freeze the actual fixture first

Use the qualified Set79 reference `testdata/public-daily/reference-v1.json` (SHA256 `a5c65673442846249b500d0db05c80652b5350ed1c032a586d275265698d25e3`) and its two-enrollment composition, together with the public baseline6 recipient catalog. Preserve Source2 limits 8 works / 8 submissions / 64MiB; Round2 8 rounds / 64MiB; ledger2 8 credits / 6 batches; both original enrollment/payee scripts and the separate operator funding script. `DailyCapacityEnvelope` must still derive ordinary maximum 2. Never increase a production cap to make the rehearsal work.

One necessary actual-only selection is a different **pool target**, independently modeled before Go expectations: expand real normal mainnet compact bits `0x207fffff` to the 32-byte target (`7fffff` followed by 29 zero bytes). The original all-ones prospect policy remains exact, as required by the existing local recipient. Every pool-winning nonce then also satisfies the actual block target. Prospect-only results still exercise the vault signer/admission/outbox but never call pool Submit and cannot consume the two pool rows. This removes the incorrect assumption that an all-ones pool target will find a block before ordinary intake fills. It does not promise that a fixed nonce wins.

Freeze a narrow producer/input recipe and independently reproduce its selected Source2, Setup2, settlement/miner/guard/scheduler bindings and remote/worker public configurations before execution. Original local binding bytes never change. Recompute every dependent remote identity explicitly; do not splice the new target under an old source ID. Select MaxRecords 64 / MaxBytes 64MiB for the new remote outbox, retaining actual limits on reopen. A bounded run that reaches this local limit before a qualifying canonical pool receipt fails; no eviction, enlarged successor or lucky-nonce retry is permitted.

The recipe freezes two exact economic branches, selected only by the final authenticated accepted-row census. Stop is requested after the first completed winning result; a second real accepted result can race that Stop. With no earlier payment/mempool fees, each credited block contributes 10 SLUG. For one accepted reward, incrementing256 receives 990,000,000 atoms, quoted fee 141 and operator change 9,999,859. For two, it receives 1,980,000,000 atoms, quoted fee 209 and change 19,999,791. The other configured gym remains zero in both branches. At the selected fixed 1,000 atoms/kVB fee, conservative native input/payee/change shapes are 113/111/563/141 (one input) and 154/220/836/209 (two inputs), stated as stripped/witness/weight/vsize. These are proposed independent arithmetic inputs to qualify, not expected bytes obtained from Go. Verify actual raw/txid, each original funding input, output and quoted fee separately; do not infer actual signature length from the conservative shape.

Fresh loopback ports, disposable TLS CA/leaf/SPKI, protected synthetic credential files and one real same-day due minute are selected and recorded before creation. Choose due = the UTC minute containing selection time + 5 minutes; refuse starts that cannot remain within the same UTC date and the fixed total budget. Every accepted reward must be mature, with the original round maintenance current, before that due minute; otherwise fail without moving it. Ledger credit import occurs through the scheduled operation, not a preparatory direct call. Runtime transport-dependent IDs are checked from the complete recorded selection using the qualified grammar; production validators are not the independent financial oracle.

## Actual sequence

1. Start exactly the two normal node processes on the copied chains, isolated to each other with DNS discovery disabled. Require the original matching nonzero tip, normal genesis/network, original bits `207fffff`, and initial height 2. Require the full scenario remains below the first 2,016-block retarget. No background mining runs. Create the fresh daily operator/schema16 wallet, rotate two distinct audience credentials for incrementing256, then Run the original runtime. Wait within existing bounds for enabled intake and public readiness before admitting worker startup.
2. Open the daily controller against the copied original root and exact original name-v1 options. Cancel the Open admission context after success, require signed-out/stopped. Login incrementing256 through the actual signed account/vault path, cancel that admission context and require a surviving original view, exact local wallet/recipient IDs, independently selected remote source ID and stopped zero-attempt child. Read the local wallet balance/height baseline through its real snapshot. Explicitly Start once using that original view.
3. Allow at most 240 seconds for actual worker discovery and delivery. Do not issue work or select nonces on its behalf. Poll only real snapshots/runtime status and the actual node. Request Stop once the node has advanced and the original snapshot shows retained records with Pending=0 plus a nonzero runtime submission count; these are a stop cue, not receipt proof. If the worker reaches derived full intake 2 first, use that exact draining/count cue and Stop even with pending admissions. No competing mining runs in this interval. Stop using the original view and join; require zero rate, with stopped or saved failed state accepted only when the exact closed evidence below passes. Record every nonempty error/code; no generic failure is silently treated as completion. Integrity, authentication, changed-source, cleanup and unexpected terminal errors fail the case. Exact busy/rate/unknown/capacity delivery states remain conditional pending evidence, not successful effects. Logout, reject the old view and Close.
4. Only after that Close, use `OpenDailyPoolOutboxAudit` and bounded List, revalidate each saved authenticated Issue work/template, and use the actual TLS Lookup endpoint for every retained pool-winning job/nonce. Require one or two distinct nonzero accepted pool receipts, contiguous accepted sequences and matching canonical node block hashes. A second outcome that raced Stop is included in all subsequent accounting. Every other row must be identified as prospect-only or an exact preserved interrupted/uncertain delivery; no uncredited row is counted as earnings. Check all immutable jobs/nonces/proofs/authorizations and every successful receipt. Require at least one actual private-vault signature under the original gym; verify every retained authorization and exact issuer receipt for every claimed accepted fighter. An additional result synchronized by an already-started hash during Stop may remain needs-signature/pending; identify it as interrupted work and preserve it, without claiming signer or birth completion for that row. A capacity-held admission is explicitly pending, never a fabricated birth. Source/issuer full census is deferred to the final closed operator audit; no raw reader overlaps the runtime. If no accepted canonical pool receipt is proved, fail. No harness Submit or replacement Issue repairs the result.
5. Reopen the same controller/local wallet/remote root/config. Require a new original view, old-view refusal and stopped state with exactly the saved immutable rows and pending count; no automatic or explicit Start on this reopen. Preserve any existing issuance hold. Retain this stopped attachment for observing the original wallet. This proves exact stopped reopen, not fresh recovery of a pending admission. Any retries already performed by the original first Run are evidenced from their actual rows; never claim an unobserved expiry or receipt after Stop.
6. With worker stopped, mine only normal uncredited helper blocks to the separate fixture address until every accepted pool coinbase has 100 descendants. Require no other pool-source earnings. A second canonical block published but not accepted before Stop is separately preserved as unresolved/uncredited; it cannot become a payout input. Helper blocks never mine/submit a retained pool job. Reach maturity before the immutable due minute; use the runtime's original round maintenance and final dated full audit to establish locks. At the real due, let only the retained runtime scheduler prepare/sign/broadcast one payout. Record the actual first raw/txid without injecting loss or altering RPC responses. Match the independently frozen one- or two-reward branch: exact accepted coinbase inputs, original incrementing256 payee, operator change and fee. Mine one further uncredited block including that transaction and wait for ordinary scheduler recovery to mark the same batch confirmed.

7. Through `NewDailyClient`, fetch bound `DailyBalance` and `PayoutsPage` for each enrollment. Require source/settlement/recipient/gym correlations, captured revision/high/before fields, one exact confirmed payment for incrementing256, and a complete empty page/zero totals for zero256. Total balances come from the complete dated report, not page summation. Separately require the stopped original local wallet is synchronized to the confirming chain and its spendable balance increased by the exact payment; RPC proves the specific output/script/txid. These are distinct wallet and pool observations.
8. Logout/Close the original controller, then join Runtime before schema16 wallet and online owner. Full `OpenDailyAudit` issuer/source/round/ledger chain and bounded public indexed projections prove exactly one or two credits matching the authenticated receipt census, one immutable batch, one exact broadcast transaction and no replacement payout. Reopen the closed outbox again for unchanged immutable rows/receipts and retained issuance hold; preserve any signed admission still pending at capacity. Compare every protected original/copy path and all source/profile/binary identities on success and failure. Stop/join both nodes. No audit races a live owner.

## Bounds and evidence

Propose the already used 900-second scenario and 1,080-second outer process bound, with original operation deadlines (30 seconds), constructor/login bounds and cleanup reservations unchanged. Worker discovery is capped at 240 seconds/64 retained rows; node chain height is capped at 180. At most two worker-published blocks + 100 maturity blocks +one confirming block keeps final height at most 105 from original height 2; record actual heights and each accepted funding height rather than requiring a particular Stop race. Logs retain the inherited 16MiB per-process cap. Outer owner controls one probe group and its exact two node children; any forced signal, leaked/unknown group, failed Close/log join or lost original descriptor fails qualification and retains the scratch tree. No alternate configuration, job or runtime is installed after a failure.

Public phases contain selected public configs/IDs, original-view snapshots, all exact public worker rows, one or two accepted canonical blocks plus any exact unresolved row, complete payment and balance/page evidence, schedule due/admission/finish wall times and joined cleanup. Private synthetic trees remain private and retained. The source catalog, compiled dependency closures, candidate no-CSE profile, normal node binary and CGO1 attachment probe are bound before/after; require the real bdb driver in the composed wallet dependency closure.

## Concrete admission edge and remaining boundaries

Current `pooloperator/capacity_drain.go:updateIntake` drains both ordinary pool and new admission intake when row2 fills the pool. `prospectworker/pool_delivery.go:deliver` submits the pool result before signing/submitting its fighter; `prospectservice/manifest_fenced_server.go:admitFenced` permits historical receipts during drain but refuses a new first receipt with `capacity`. The worker correctly retains this signed admission as pending. A first admission can therefore be held even for the winning row that filled the pool, and old signed-but-not-yet-admitted rows can remain held too. Requiring Pending=0 or every fighter accepted would be a timing-dependent harness assumption. This plan can prove original signatures, exact pending preservation and the scheduled payment without claiming every fighter birth. If full fighter completion at the boundary is required, root must first select a narrow product contract for retained issued-work admission/headroom; do not change financial capacity, reorder product delivery or weaken admission guards in the harness. There is no automatic new-job or hold-reset workaround.

No missing product accessor is required for this plan: the concrete controller snapshot, closed outbox audit, current daily HTTP reads and full closed ledger audits suffice. The independent block-target/config/economic fixture is now qualified (a48a854d); the source-bound harness remains unexecuted pending review and root authorization. Direct controller composition does not by itself qualify the new headless `slugpilot --daily` argv/process path; that can be checked separately without inventing a daily helper protocol. Only incrementing256 is exercised; honoring zero256's hold is intentional. This case proves one original-wallet automatic mining/payment cycle, not public hosting, continuous 64-miner load, all retained capacity, V2 fighter ownership/history adoption, transfers/recovery, general login/onboarding or D74 release readiness. Path B retains the independent ordinary-target/late-winner/reserved-payout obligations.
